- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., 80+), especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If true price drops sharply after a forecast peak, model may be lagging — adjust downward by 5–10% of the forecasted peak in the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +1 to -1) triggers downward correction: reduce forecast by 3–7% immediately, then apply 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and price is trending, model often misses direction — use 3-day moving average of history to anchor forecast.
